name: Sir John Davies
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Sir John Davies was an English poet, lawyer and politician who later served as Attorney General for Ireland.
He is best remembered for ‘Nosce Teipsum,’ a long philosophical poem on the nature of the soul, and for witty, compact epigrams on the paradox of human self-knowledge.

poems.title: Man
poems.author: Sir John Davies
poems.text:
I know my soul hath power to know all things,
    Yet she is blind and ignorant in all:
    I know I’m one of Nature’s little kings,
    Yet to the least and vilest things am thrall.

    I know my life’s a pain and but a span;
    I know my sense is mock’d in everything;
    And, to conclude, I know myself a Man--
    Which is a proud and yet a wretched thing.
